issues.legal_issue: A lessee’s sustained voluntary interruption of mining operations and neglect that endangers the mine can justify termination of the lease after notice and failure to remedy the breach.
material_facts: The lease required the lessee to continue mining without voluntary intermission and to work skilfully and in a workmanlike manner.
Work stopped after the partners failed to fund operations, wages went unpaid, and essential services ceased.
The mine began to flood when the pumps stopped; government intervention saved it.
The lessee did not remedy the defects within the notice period or seek an extension.
issues.conclusion: The lessee breached its obligations and endangered the mine by neglect, entitling the State Government to determine the lease.
issues.legal_principle: The lease covenant required continuous work without voluntary intermission. Rule 27(1)(f) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 required proper, skilful and workmanlike operations, and Rule 27(5) empowered the State Government to give notice to remedy a breach and, upon default, determine the lease. The Court also referred to the corresponding power under Rule 41 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949.

rule.if: mining_lease_determination_case and lease_operation_duty_breached and (voluntary_work_interruption or negligent_mine_endangerment) and notice_to_remedy_given and breach_not_remedied

predicates.mining_lease_determination_case: The proceeding concerns whether a mining lease may be determined because the lessee failed to operate the mine as required.
predicates.lease_operation_duty_breached: The lessee failed to meet its obligation to continue mining operations in a proper and workmanlike manner.
predicates.voluntary_work_interruption: Mining work stopped for a sustained period because the lessee failed to keep operations running.
predicates.negligent_mine_endangerment: The lessee’s neglect caused conditions that threatened serious damage to or loss of the mine.
predicates.notice_to_remedy_given: The government gave the lessee notice requiring the operational breach to be remedied.
predicates.breach_not_remedied: The lessee did not remedy the breach within the time allowed and did not obtain an extension.

issues.definition: When a lease-determination proceeding concerns a breached duty to operate a mine, and the lessee’s interruption or neglect endangers it and remains unremedied after notice, lease determination is justified.

issues.legal_issue: In a revision proceeding, the reviewing government may reject the application after obtaining the State Government’s comments and giving the applicant an opportunity to respond, and need not provide a detailed order where the facts are clear and the supported decision is being affirmed.
material_facts: The lessee applied to the Central Government for revision of the State Government’s decision to take over the mine and terminate the lease.
The Central Government obtained the State Government’s comments and invited the lessee to comment on them.
The material facts concerning the stoppage of work, unpaid wages, cessation of essential services, and danger of flooding were clear.
The Central Government rejected the revision, approving the State Government’s action.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed revision procedure was followed, the lessee had an opportunity to respond to the State Government’s comments, and a detailed order was not required in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The Mineral Concession Rules required the Central Government to obtain the State Government’s comments on a revision application and to give the applicant an opportunity to make representations on those comments. Harinagar Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Shyam Sundar Jhunjhunwala established the general requirement to give reasons in quasi-judicial decisions; Madhya Pradesh Industries Ltd. v. Union of India held that an order affirming an earlier decision need not repeat its reasons. Aluminium Corporation of India Ltd. v. Union of India was distinguished because the decision there relied on a report received behind the affected party’s back and did not explain rejection of part of that party’s case.

rule.if: government_revision_case and state_comments_obtained and applicant_given_opportunity_to_respond and material_facts_clear and review_affirms_supported_decision

predicates.government_revision_case: The proceeding is an administrative revision of a government decision affecting a mining lease.
predicates.state_comments_obtained: The reviewing government obtained the State Government’s comments on the revision application.
predicates.applicant_given_opportunity_to_respond: The reviewing government invited the applicant to respond to the State Government’s comments.
predicates.material_facts_clear: The record clearly established the material events underlying the decision under review.
predicates.review_affirms_supported_decision: The reviewing government affirmed a decision supported by the record.

issues.definition: In a government revision proceeding, where the State Government’s comments are obtained, the applicant can respond, the material facts are clear, and the supported decision is affirmed, the process may be sufficient without detailed reasons.
